PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached, and no hardware or real-MuJoCo run is claimed. The card's entry symbol deploy.deploy_mujoco53:main exists at deploy/deploy_mujoco53.py:1915 (confirmed by AST). It is a viewer-coupled script: it requires a positional config_file (line 1919), loads the MJCF named by deploy/config/g1_53.yaml with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path (line 1937), assigns model.opt.timestep from the config (line 1939), opens mujoco.viewer.launch_passive (line 1993) and advances the model with mujoco.mj_step (line 2044), exposing no reset or step API of its own. The card's decision family-config and helper MujocoDriver are used as written: this package serves the card's models[0], resources/g1/scene53.xml, through MujocoDriver, so there is no deviation from the card. The read-only clone was read in place for parsing only; it was not modified and no file of it was written. The served scene includes resources/g1/g1_53dof.xml; it has 83 qpos and 79 qvel values (three scene free bodies, two drawer slide joints, the robot free base and 53 robot hinges) and 53 motor actuators (resources/g1/g1_53dof.xml:812-887). None of the 53 motors declares a ctrlrange, so the bridge derives no per-actuator control bound; the model's joint ranges and actuatorfrcrange values constrain joint positions and torques in MuJoCo, not the data.ctrl value that cap.world.step.v1 writes, and this package does not invent one. The scene also adds three free-floating bodies and two drawer slides (resources/g1/scene53.xml:39-133); the fake holds them fixed, while the real engine would simulate them. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed here (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is the package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as FakeMujoco. It parses the same scene and its include for the joint shape, the 53 actuators, the free bodies, the drawer slides and the deployed 0.002 s step, but its integration is a placeholder (a fixed gain times each control value for the actuated hinges and slides); it loads no STL mesh or texture, resolves no contact, inertia, gravity, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics, and implements no mj_getState/mj_setState, so the bridge's fallback copy is the snapshot path. The fidelity gaps list every difference; no trajectory was compared with the real engine and no hardware was validated. The real mujoco path (a backend name that backends does not list) was not run. WARNINGS kept from the last gate run (none of them failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED, because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library rather than a package object the gate can wrap in a Recorder, so native calls are not recorded; G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, because the fake is a stand-in for the mujoco library, so the gate has no fake class surface to check; G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, which reports CL2 on that one check because the driver declares no limit on any actuating capability (the model has no ctrlrange, so there is no sourced bound to declare); and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs seed, ticks and action.ctrl[*], which are expected for simulator families. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds seven cases (scene shape and pelvis/box/glass start positions from the MJCF, control-vector length, step advancing the integration state, reset to model defaults, reset seed accepted without changing the model (the MuJoCo bridge does not use it), published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
